en: The Philippines has 7,641 islands, not the commonly cited 7,107, according to the updated NAMRIA count.
The Cagayan River, not the Pasig River, is the longest river in the Philippines at approximately 505 kilometers.
Lake Mainit in Mindanao, not Laguna de Bay, is the deepest lake in the Philippines at about 113 meters.
Mount Apo in Davao, standing at 2,954 meters, is the highest mountain in the Philippines, not Mount Mayon.
The Philippine Sea lies on the eastern side of the country, while the South China Sea is on the western side.
The famous Chocolate Hills are located in the province of Bohol, not in Cebu.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were built by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago, not by Spanish colonizers.
The Philippines has 24 active volcanoes because it sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, not zero.
Davao City is the largest city in the Philippines by land area, not Manila.
Quezon City, not Manila, is the most populous city in the Philippines.
Taal Volcano sits on Volcano Island in the middle of Taal Lake in Batangas, not on the mainland.
Palawan is part of the MIMAROPA region under the Luzon island group, not the Visayas.
